authority: uvp-core uvp-ir::canonical_stringify (serde_json integer number identity; float-form literals rejected at the authority)
consumers: uvp-core uvp-ir::canonical_stringify is authoritative for every expectCanonical case: Rust accepts integer literals across the full u64/i64 range and emits them bare.

uvp-protocol packages/compiler canonical.ts must reproduce every expectCanonical case byte-for-byte and reject expectReject cases with an equivalent single rejection face. A case carrying expectTsReject is the explicit cross-track exception: TS numbers are limited to ±(2^53-1), so TS must reject that input loudly as an unsafe integer and must not claim byte-for-byte alignment with the Rust u64 vector.
rules: The canonical hash-preimage vocabulary is closed over integers: number literals without '.' or 'e' (u64/i64) canonicalize bare, without a decimal point.

Integer width is split by track: the Rust authority accepts u64/i64 integer tokens exactly, including values above JS's safe-integer range (> 2^53-1); JS/TS consumers accept only safe integers and must reject larger tokens loudly. A case with expectTsReject is a Rust-only acceptance vector and a TS rejection vector, not a cross-track byte-alignment obligation.

Float-form number literals are rejected outright by both tracks: any f64 payload — integral floats (100.0), fractions (1.5), exponent spellings (1e2, 2.5e-8, 1e300), and negative zero (-0.0) — fails loudly at the authoritative canonicalizer, listing the offending token. Cross-language float formatting (ryu vs JS Number->String) carries no byte-for-byte alignment obligation; the single rejection face lives in the Rust authority.
Object keys sort by code point; arrays keep order.

cases.name: integer token stays a bare integer
max safe integer stays an integer on both tracks
u64 beyond double precision is a Rust acceptance vector and a TS safe-integer rejection
keys sort by code point over integers
exponent spelling is a float and is rejected
negative zero is a float and is rejected
small scientific float nested in an array is rejected
large scientific float nested deep in an object is rejected
integer literal beyond the 64-bit range parses as an f64 payload and is rejected
the first offending float is reported deterministically in sorted-key order
